sulfur_reference_anchors.citation_caveat: IMPORTANT: the ligand is VANILLIN, not 2-furfurylthiol - the word 'furfuryl' does not occur anywhere in the paper. The entry's compounds_supported ('2-furfurylthiol') is therefore wrong and the -9.72 kcal/mol value must not be used as an FFT binding energy. Also note -9.72 kcal/mol is the thermodynamic delta-G from binding isotherms, not the docking score (the docking affinities are -3.9689 kcal/mol for PPI and -3.7660 for deamidated PPI), so the entry's note 'obtained via molecular docking and homology modeling' is also inaccurate.

source_status_repair.basis: The backlog page reference 'JAFC 39:1207' is fabricated: I enumerated all CrossRef records for JAFC volume 39 pages 1195-1220 and p.1207 falls inside Mirvish et al., 'N-Nitrosoatrazine: synthesis, kinetics of formation...', JAFC 39:1205-1210 (10.1021/jf00007a002) - no HDMF paper occupies that page. CrossRef author search for Blank+Grosch 1990-1993 returns only 'Evaluation of Potent Odorants in Dill Seed and Dill Herb by Aroma Extract Dilution Analysis', J. Food Sci. 56:63-67 (10.1111/j.1365-2621.1991.tb07976.x) - not HDMF, not boiled beef. Neither the SLR anchors ('HDMF ODT 0.003 ppb', '78% from ribose+glucose') nor the backlog anchors ('HDMF in boiled beef 28-67 ug/kg, OAV 4.7-11.2') can be tied to any Blank & Grosch 1991 publication. | Nearest genuine Blank sources on HDMF, neither of which is 1991 nor supplies these numbers: Blank & Fay (1996), 'Formation of 4-Hydroxy-2,5-dimethyl-3(2H)-furanone and 4-Hydroxy-2(or 5)-ethyl-5(or 2)-methyl-3(2H)-furanone through Maillard Reaction Based on Pentose Sugars', JAFC 44:531-536, doi:10.1021/jf950439o; and Blank, Fay, Lakner & Schlosser (1997), JAFC 45:2642-2648, doi:10.1021/jf960997i (SIDA quantification of HDMF/HEMF in pentose Maillard model systems). Do not attach the 0.003 ppb threshold to either without reading them.

furanone_reference_anchors.notes: Quantifies HDMF from iso-oligosaccharides (3.8 ug/g) and maltose (1.4 ug/g) at 140 C without amino acids.

source_status_repair.basis: The DOI stem is impossible: ACS Symposium Series volume 740 is 'Surfactant-Based Separations' (CrossRef 10.1021/bk-2000-0740.ch001, Scamehorn & Harwell), not a flavour/HDMF volume, and no 10.1021/bk-1999-0740.* chapter exists. 'Hauck & Tressl' is a chimera of two unrelated groups: Tobias Hauck published on HDMF with Wilfried Schwab (e.g. Hauck, Landmann, Raab, Bruhlmann & Schwab (2002), Carbohydr. Res. 337:1185-1191, 10.1016/s0008-6215(02)00121-0), while Roland Tressl's 1999 output is 'Heat Generated Flavors and Precursors' with Rewicki (Flavor Chemistry, 10.1007/978-1-4615-4693-1_26). Neither reports HDMF yields of 3.8 / 1.4 / 2.9 ug/g from iso-oligosaccharides, maltose and methylglyoxal self-condensation at 140 C; repeated CrossRef searches on those terms find nothing. | If a non-amino-acid HDMF-formation anchor is needed, Hauck et al. (2002) Carbohydr. Res. 337:1185-1191 (10.1016/s0008-6215(02)00121-0) genuinely shows chemical HDMF formation from D-fructose-1,6-diphosphate without amino acids - but from a phosphorylated sugar, not from oligosaccharides/maltose, and without the repo's ug/g values.

doi_repair.basis: Round-2 recovery high confidence: CrossRef search for 'epigallocatechin gallate trapping deoxyosone xylose alanine Maillard' surfaced the SI record 10.1021/acs.jafc.0c00200.s001; the parent record and the PubMed abstract (PMID 31957424) confirm both of the repo's numeric anchors exactly: EGCG lowers the activation energy for xylose/alanine -> ARP conversion 'from 77.8 to 62.8 kJ/mol' (= 15.0 kJ/mol reduction) and improves the ARP (N-(1-deoxy-D-xylulos-1-yl)alanine) yield 'from 2 to 95%'. The matrix (xylose/alanine model system), the compound, and the EGCG-trapping-of-deoxyosones mechanism all match the SLR entry.

source_status_repair.basis: I enumerated every CrossRef record for JAFC (ISSN 0021-8561) published in 2014 (1561 items) and checked first pages: no article starts at p. 10295. Page 10295 falls inside Granato et al., JAFC 62:10283-10296 (10.1021/jf504480f, antioxidant extraction / response surface), and the next article begins at 10297 (Trujillo et al., nitrohydroxytyrosol). Separately, a CrossRef author sweep shows Gloria Marquez-Ruiz has no JAFC paper in 2014 at all (her 2014 output is in Eur. J. Lipid Sci. Technol. and Lipid Technol.), and no 'high-oleic olive oil frying volatiles with OAVs for 8 compounds' paper by her exists. | Both the venue coordinates and the author/year are fabricated, so the 'nonanal ODT 1.0 ppb / OAV 1-28' anchor has no source behind it. Note also that the SLR entry says matrix 'oleic_model' while the backlog says 'high-oleic olive oil frying' - internally inconsistent. If a real high-oleic frying-volatile anchor is wanted, Huang et al. (2024), Food Res. Int. 192:114749 (10.1016/j.foodres.2024.114749) covers volatile aldehyde distribution in high-oleic sunflower oil during frying, but it is a different paper and I did not verify the OAV numbers in it.

source_status_repair.basis: The current DOI is definitively wrong: 10.1021/jf00111a008 is Purcell & Walter (1982), 'Stability of amino acids during cooking and processing of sweet potatoes'. The work actually meant by 'Grosch (1982)' in the lipid-oxidation literature is the Elsevier book chapter above - it is a real, widely-cited chapter (CrossRef indexes only a 1982 Food Chemistry review OF the book, 10.1016/0308-8146(82)90085-1, not the chapter itself), and it carries no DOI. It is also not a JAFC paper as the repo backlog claims. | I could NOT confirm that the specific value hexanal ODT = 4.5 ppb appears in Grosch (1982). Published hexanal odour thresholds in water span 0.3-14 ug/L across studies, so 4.5 ppb is in range but unattributed. The nearest verifiable primary source for hexanal thresholds from Grosch's own group is Ullrich & Grosch (1987), 'Identification of the most intense volatile flavour compounds formed during autoxidation of linoleic acid', Z. Lebensm. Unters. Forsch. 184:277-282, DOI 10.1007/BF01027663 - but I could not read its threshold table (Springer paywall), so I do not assert it contains 4.5 ppb. Treat the hexanal ODT as unsourced until the value is read off a table.

Technol. and Lipid Technol.), and no 'high-oleic olive oil frying volatiles with OAVs for 8 compounds' paper by her exists. | Both the venue coordinates and the author/year are fabricated, so the 'nonanal ODT 1.0 ppb / OAV 1-28' anchor has no source behind it. Note also that the SLR entry says matrix 'oleic_model' while the backlog says 'high-oleic olive oil frying' - internally inconsistent. If a real high-oleic frying-volatile anchor is wanted, Huang et al. (2024), Food Res. Int. 192:114749 (10.1016/j.foodres.2024.114749) covers volatile aldehyde distribution in high-oleic sunflower oil during frying, but it is a different paper and I did not verify the OAV numbers in it.

Enumerated Yeo & Shibamoto's 1991 output via CrossRef author search: all of it is microwave Maillard model-system work - 'Effects of moisture content on the Maillard browning model system upon microwave irradiation' (JAFC 39:1860, 10.1021/jf00010a035), 'Microwave-induced volatiles of the Maillard model system under different pH conditions' (JAFC 39:370, 10.1021/jf00002a029), 'Flavor and browning enhancement by electrolytes during microwave irradiation of the Maillard model system' (JAFC 39:948, 10.1021/jf00005a030). None concerns warmed-over flavour, phospholipid-derived hexanal, or lipoxygenase thermal inactivation. Targeted searches for the anchors (phospholipid fraction 82-88% of hexanal; LOX D-value 28 min) returned nothing. | The entry fuses two unrelated claims under a citation that supports neither. For the phospholipid-dominance phenomenon the canonical anchor is Igene & Pearson (1979), 'Role of Phospholipids and Triglycerides in Warmed-Over Flavor Development in Meat Model Systems', J. Food Sci. 44:1285-1290, doi 10.1111/j.1365-2621.1979.tb06420.x - but I did NOT confirm the 82-88% figure in it, and it says nothing about a 28 min LOX D-value, which needs a separate lipoxygenase thermal-inactivation source.

The repo's 'Cys blocking rate 2.9x faster than Lys' and '43% Lys blocked at 10:1 ratio' are NOT in this paper and could not be traced to any publication - treat them as unsourced.
